book: Quantitative Aptitude for Competitive Examinations — R.S. Aggarwal

key_explanation_from_book.clock_face: The clock face is divided into 60 equal minute spaces. The hour hand completes one revolution in 12 hours and the minute hand completes one revolution in 1 hour.
key_explanation_from_book.angles: Minute hand moves 6° per minute. Hour hand moves 30° per hour, or 1/2° per minute.
key_explanation_from_book.angle_formula: At H hours and M minutes, the angle between the hands is |30H - 11M/2| degrees; the smaller angle is taken when required.
key_explanation_from_book.coincidence: The hands coincide 11 times in every 12 hours, hence 22 times in a day.
key_explanation_from_book.right_angle: The hands are at right angles 22 times in every 12 hours, hence 44 times in a day.
key_explanation_from_book.opposite: The hands are in a straight line but opposite in direction 11 times in every 12 hours.
key_explanation_from_book.gain_loss: For a clock gaining or losing time, compare its indicated rate with the correct rate to determine the actual time.
key_explanation_from_book.interval: The minute hand gains on the hour hand at 55 minute-spaces per hour, which is used to calculate coincidence and separation times.
